item.text: The Crime and Corruption Commission surveyed Queensland council employees to assess perceived corruption risks, reporting barriers and opportunities for prevention.
item.support: pinpoint barriers to reporting corruption and suspected wrongdoing among local government employees

item.text: The online survey ran from mid-May to early June 2020 and analysed responses from more than 6500 employees across 68 councils.
item.support: Analysed survey responses from over 6500 local government employees across 68 councils

item.text: The CCC reported that employees more often perceived corruption in the wider sector than in their own workplace, and identified misuse of authority and conflicts of interest as common concerns.
item.support:
Most local government employees identified 
that corruption occurs and is a problem 
in the broader local government sector.

item.text: The CCC reported strong willingness to report corruption, alongside uncertainty about reporting channels and concerns about management inaction, careers and workplace relationships.
item.support:

item.text: The CCC called for targeted reporting education, support from managers and accessible, practical internal guidance.
item.support:
Local governments should ensure their internal resources are accessible, 
up-to-date and provide clear and practical advice to their employees.
